title: Prove the V4 trusted host and four-root boundary
goal: Implement a local V4 P0 spike in which a .NET host safely runs one hash-bound synthetic PowerShell adapter using four explicit roots and produces equivalent structured verdicts from in-repository and separated package locations without changing V3, IFX or remote governance.
acceptanceCriteria: The canonical V4 repository root spelling is docs/guards/v4 and the spike has a package-local .NET 10 build baseline with no external package dependency.
The host requires and canonicalizes PackageRoot, TargetRoot, StateRoot and EvidenceRoot and rejects unsafe overlap, path escape and links or reparse points.
The synthetic PowerShell adapter is selected by registered module ID, hash-verified and denied before execution when it requests a target write or another undeclared capability.
Only the host writes the normalized schema-valid result below EvidenceRoot; package and target authority hashes do not change.
In-repository and separated exact package copies produce equivalent normalized verdicts for the same synthetic target.
Hash drift, capability escalation, unsafe roots and malformed adapter output are structured fail-closed outcomes with stable preliminary exit categories.
Current V3 Validate and ifx-package-test remain green and no current workflow, required check, V3/V3_ifx authority or remote state changes.
